description.narrative:
Project Outcomes Stakeholder effects Increased access to finance for financially stressed companies: The Project will provide up to US$300 million financing in loans to mid-market companies, enabling them to recover their business operations, avoid liquidation, and preserve jobs.
Stakeholder effects Enable Financial Institutions (FIs) Dispose non-performing loans (NPLs) and borrowers to normalize their obligations: NPLs pose challenges for both lenders and borrowers as they restrict credit availability, disrupt credit allocation, erode market confidence, and hinder economic growth. In this context, the Fund will acquire NPLs from FIs and allow them to release capital and thus increase their capacity to lend. The Project will also reduce the costs, for FIs, of managing these distressed assets and refocus their attention to their core lending activities. Through this Project, IFC will also help to bring the financially distressed but viable businesses in the target countries back to creditworthiness and regain access to finance, while preserving jobs.
Contribution to Market Creation Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that the Project will promote greater competitiveness in the distressed assets and special situations financing segment, by supporting the development of an alternate financing channel like private credit funds in this segment. Through demonstration and replication, IFC expects that the Project will attract potential investors and new funds in the private credit space to enter and crowd-in more private capital to scale up lending to distressed assets and special situations, contributing to the secondary market development across Asia. By supporting the growth and expansion of GICAM, IFC will demonstrate the viability of providing special situations financing to businesses and will encourage other players to enter this segment.

The proposed project entails an IFC investment as an anchor investor in Asia Debt Opportunities Fund II (ADOF II or the Fund). The Fund will focus on distressed debt, special situations, asset-backed credit portfolios as well as single assets and will have a life of up to 8 years. ADOF II will be managed by GI Capital Management Ltd (GICAM or the Company), a Japan-based manager with US$754 million of Assets under Management (AUM) and over 20 years of credit experience. The Fund is targeted at US$300 million, with first close aimed at US$100 million. IFCs investment is proposed at the lower of up to US$30 million or up to 15% of the Fund commitments. ADOF IIs geographical scope will be pan-Asia spanning across various sectors and asset classes.
